main_text.p: vafit, velut omnis jam spes restitutionis infelicibus istis simul ac semel esset ademta: præsertim vero in Achaiâ, ubi cunctorum mentes in profundum mœrorem & desperationem sunt versæ: quemadmodum contra, Callicrates & Charopus, & qui istius erant factionis, animos supra modum extulerunt.

Post aliquot deinde annos, cum jam longè plurimos evocatorum, ac penè omnes, quibus celebrius nomen erat, præsertim natu grandes, fatum in Italiâ consumpsisset, rursum legati ex Achaia Romam venere, ut pro iis, qui superstites adhuc erant, intercederent, Xeno & Telecles, idque potissimum ob Polybium historiæ scriptorem, qui ante alios cum patre Lycorta delatus à Callicrate fuerat, & Stratium Trittæensem. Horum autem legatorum mandata, quæ domo attulerant, erant puræ putæ preces, ne disputando & contentendo senatus offenderetur. Sed & sic nihil profectum;[illegible, ~2 letters] Tam obstinatis animis Romani tum fuêre, ut Callicratem patriæ pestem foverent, & Achæos obedire potentioribus docerent. Iterum tamen legati ab Achæis missi: & hi flexis jam multorum animis in spem venerant impetrandæ dimissionis: sed fraude Posthu-mii prætoris Romani, qui absentibus

page.notes: Left margin carries a column of printed pointing-hand (manicule) ornaments; these are not text and are not transcribed. The marginal mark beside "profectum" is small and unclear; it is shown as illegible. The catchword at the foot is partly cut off and uncertain. The final word of the page is cut at the line end as printed. Right edge shows the book's red edge and the lower right corner shows a faint edge fragment, which were left out.
